intro: Searching for sedation dentistry near me usually means you or someone you care for feels anxious about dental treatment and wants to know what options are available locally. You may be putting off a check-up or a procedure because of fear, or you might need help finding a practice that offers sedation. We introduce you to a private dentist who can talk you through sedation and quote you directly.
need_heading: What people searching for sedation dentistry near me usually need
need_lead: Most people who search for sedation dentistry near me are looking for a local practice that offers sedation and can help them manage dental anxiety.
needs: You feel so anxious about the dentist that you have delayed treatment and want to find a practice that offers sedation to make it easier.
You have a strong gag reflex or a previous bad experience and want to know whether sedation could help you get through a filling or extraction.
You need a longer procedure and want to discuss whether intravenous, oral or inhalation sedation would suit you.
You are looking for a dentist near you who can explain the sedation options and what the day will involve.
You want to understand how sedation is provided safely and what you need to do before and after your appointment.
context_heading: What to understand about sedation dentistry
context: Sedation dentistry uses medicines to help you relax during treatment. It is not the same as a general anaesthetic, and you will usually remain conscious and able to respond. Private dentists who offer sedation should have appropriate training, and you can ask about their experience and the team's training.

Dentists and dental care professionals must be registered with the General Dental Council (GDC), and you can check the register online. Private clinics providing regulated healthcare in England must register with the Care Quality Commission (CQC), which inspects and publishes ratings. In Wales the regulator is Healthcare Inspectorate Wales, in Scotland Healthcare Improvement Scotland, and in Northern Ireland the RQIA.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Explain how you feel about dental treatment and what has stopped you going, so we can introduce you to a dentist who understands anxiety.
Mention any previous sedation you have had and whether it worked well or caused any problems.
Say what treatment you think you need, such as a check-up, filling, extraction or a longer procedure.
Tell us about any medical conditions or medicines you take, as these can affect sedation choices.
Let us know if you need to be accompanied home after sedation or have caring responsibilities that affect your day.
Confirm how far you are willing to travel and whether you need appointments at a particular time of day.
questions: What type of sedation do you offer, and how do you decide which is right for me?
What training and experience do you and your team have in providing sedation?
What should I do before the appointment, and can I eat or drink beforehand?
Will I need someone to escort me home, and how long should I plan to rest afterwards?
What are the risks and side effects of the sedation you recommend?
What happens if I feel anxious on the day or the sedation does not work as expected?

faqs.a: Sedation dentistry is generally safe when provided by trained professionals who assess your health first. Your dentist should discuss your medical history and any medicines you take before recommending a type of sedation. Ask about the team's training and what monitoring is used during treatment.

faqs.q: Will I be asleep during sedation?
faqs.a: Most sedation used in dentistry makes you relaxed and drowsy rather than fully asleep. You will usually be able to respond to the dentist, but you may remember little of the appointment. The type of sedation and its effect will be explained to you beforehand.

faqs.q: Can I drive home after having sedation?
faqs.a: You should not drive or operate machinery for a period after sedation, so you will need someone to take you home. Plan your day around recovery and follow the practice's instructions about when you can resume normal activities.

faqs.q: How do I find a sedation dentist near me?
faqs.a: You can search for local practices that offer sedation, but it is worth asking about their training and experience. We introduce you to a private dentist who can discuss sedation with you and provide a quote. You can also check the dentist's registration with the General Dental Council.
